definitions.meaning: read as two words plus a phrase, a stall or display ... at a seafood show

explanation.surface: A chilled section of a seafood exhibition, perhaps the bit on ice.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the answer into STAND OF FISH, a display at a seafood show; 'Cool' looks like temperature but means aloof.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cool towards others is aloof and distant, holding people at arm's length.

clue.text: Sulphur's abrasive — must protect eye immediately

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

indicators.note: one word guarding another means it wraps round it, so the private eye sits inside

parts.note: abrasive in manner means harsh
a private eye is a PI, a private investigator

explanation.surface: A warning that sulphur is abrasive and you must shield your eyes at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye' tempts toward I, but it is a private eye, a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something sharpish is a colloquial British way of saying quickly or at once.

clue.text: A couple of pages before index, perhaps?

definitions.text: A couple of pages before index, perhaps?
definitions.note: a supplementary section of a few pages placed at the back of a book, just ahead of the index

indicators.note: the first pieces come ahead of the rest

parts.note: P is page, so two of them are PP

indicators.note: a maybe-version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bookbinder noting a few pages placed ahead of the index.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is the anagram signal on the final word; read whole, the clue also describes where supplementary pages sit in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplementary material at the back of a book commonly sits just ahead of its index, so the clue describes it.

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top, held up by what comes below it

parts.note: a dissolute man is a rake, a libertine

explanation.surface: A daughter being kept by a debauched adventurer.
explanation.walkthrough: A rake is a dissolute man, here standing in for the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan seafarer who circumnavigated the globe.

definitions.meaning: to stamp off is to storm out in a temper
a fluid ounce, abbreviated fl oz, is one twentieth of an imperial pint

explanation.surface: A postage stamp showing a tiny measure of liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as FL OUNCE, a fluid ounce, which is one twentieth of a British imperial pint.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounce is to move off in an angry, exaggerated huff, just as one might stamp away.

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: info is information, news
a secondhand item is used

explanation.surface: Most of the news reported is recycled, poured in from elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' docks the last letter of INFO, leaving INF.
explanation.definitionFit: Something infused has been steeped or poured into a liquid or a situation.

definitions.meaning: judges hand down sentences, so the phrase also describes passing judgment

explanation.surface: A judge turning out sentences with no trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning without any difficulty is winning by a comfortable margin, an idiom from horse racing.

parts.note: it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A homily that generosity is a virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is old slang for sex appeal, SA. 'give' is a verb here: a beam or rope gives when it yields.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor or shelf that sags yields or gives way under weight.

clue.text: Alpine course seen in flm about sport

indicators.note: one piece placed round another, so the film wraps the sport

parts.note: a printed slip for film: a thin layer or film is a skin
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A downhill route shown in a movie about a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flm' is a typo for 'film', a skin. 'seen in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste in the Alps is a track for skiers to descend.

indicators.note: dressed in something means wrapped by it, so the editor goes inside

parts.note: drab colours are grey
ED is an editor, the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A hungry reporter dressed in dull clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drably' is an adverb in the surface but supplies the drab colour; 'attired' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenous or starving hunger makes one avid to eat everything, a sense of greed.

indicators.note: the pub sits inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: ALA is the older abbreviation for Alabama
PH is a public house on maps

explanation.surface: A tavern located in the state of Alabama.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the lone letter 'A', which looks like a mere article.
explanation.definitionFit: The NATO phonetic alphabet's code word for the letter A, and the first Greek letter.

parts.note: to off someone is slang for killing them

indicators.note: losing its head means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: deep in thought is pensive

explanation.surface: A horrid killing, with the thought of decapitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' strips the P from PENSIVE, leaving ENSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offensive is unpleasant or objectionable, as nasty remarks are.

parts.note: to author a text is to pen it

indicators.note: turned about means read backwards

parts.note: one who sinned did wrong

explanation.surface: A writer was mistaken about a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the reversal signal. 'Author' is a verb, to write, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray's Pendennis is a Victorian work of fiction.

definitions.meaning: a ... sleep is a deep one

explanation.surface: A water source sunk deep.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: unbroken, profound sleep and healthy, robust condition.

indicators.note: a tipsy speaker slurs s into sh, so the word for one is said drunkenly

parts.note: a single is one

explanation.surface: A roofer asking whether a tile is snugly fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' is slang for drunk: a drunk says SINGLE as SHINGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingles are wooden roof tiles.

indicators.note: one piece holding another inside

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
ribald humour is coarse and rude

explanation.surface: A coarse soldier taking a nationalist prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi led the struggle to unify Italy and is honoured as a national hero.

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
an operation is an op

explanation.surface: Leaving the GP's practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surgery' suggests a doctor's premises, but it is an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a plan or a person is to abandon them.

clue.text: When it penetrates skin it sucks blood

indicators.note: piercing a word means going inside it

parts.note: to pare is to peel or skin
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: A description of a tick or leech biting through the skin to feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skin' is a verb, pare, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick or leech is an organism that feeds off a host, here by taking blood.

clue.text: Street location situated beyond unnamed river

indicators.note: the next piece comes after the others

parts.note: some person is an unnamed one
set means placed or located

explanation.surface: A road lying past a river with no name.
explanation.walkthrough: Street is a town in the English county of Somerset, so 'Street' is not a road.
explanation.definitionFit: The town of Street lies in this south-west English county.

clue.text: Weakling died — these letters prove it

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, on a gravestone shows death

explanation.surface: A feeble person has died, as gravestone lettering confirms.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is a colloquial term for a feeble, wet person.

clue.text: Cards most unlikely to be used in snap

indicators.note: put to use inside another word, so it goes within

parts.note: a snap is a photo, a pic
the last person to do something is the least likely

explanation.surface: Playing cards that would never appear in a game of snap, the simple children's card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snap' suggests the card game, but it is a photograph, PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit and debit cards are collectively called by the material they are made of.

clue.text: Foreign money, once exchanged, includes returned tax

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
the letters swapped round
sent back means read backwards

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Overseas currency changed once includes tax refunded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanged' scrambles the word once to CENO; 'returned' turns the tax backwards, and 'includes' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A centavo is a small coin of Latin American currencies.

indicators.note: taking something in, so a goes into the councillor

parts.note: the Toon is a nickname for Newcastle and its football club

explanation.surface: A local councillor takes on a Newcastle football shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: A strip is a football kit, but here it is a comic strip. TOON is Geordie slang for Newcastle, a city in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic strip is a series of drawn panels.

clue.text: Last part of anagram indicator in essence

indicators.note: the final letter of the word

parts.note: an arrow points or indicates

explanation.surface: A crossword note on the final bit of an anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The marrow of something is its vital core or essence.

parts.note: to flag is to tire or sink
on means continuing, as in keep on

explanation.surface: A fortress sinking a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' is not a castle tower: it means carry on, ON. 'sinking' is FLAG, wilting.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jug or bottle for drink, a vessel.

indicators.note: a typo for backfires: fires back means reads backwards

parts.note: Bild is a German tabloid
A is an indefinite article

explanation.surface: A German tabloid story misfires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfres' reverses BILD A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad-lib remark is improvised, made up on the spot.

clue.text: Rope knotted, in a way, for crate?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go inside

parts.note: a lane is a way

indicators.note: tied in a knot, the letters are twisted

explanation.surface: A rope tied in some way to secure a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knotted' scrambles the rope's letters, which sit inside A LANE. Crate is old RAF slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Crate is old slang for an aircraft, especially a ramshackle one.

clue.text: After training, is about to quaff soft drink

indicators.note: drinking something down takes it inside, so the pieces swallow the soft letter
the turned word follows the physical training

parts.note: PE is physical education, training

indicators.note: turned about means read backwards

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Someone after a workout is about to gulp a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft' seems to belong to 'soft drink', but it is the musical marking piano; 'to quaff' takes it inside, and 'about' turns the word is.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known brand of cola, one kind of drink.

clue.text: Fiddle, primarily one hired for opera

parts.note: to rig is to fiddle a result

indicators.note: only the leading letter of the next word

parts.note: let means rented out
to is for, as in 'a gift for you' and 'given to you'

explanation.surface: A fiddler, chiefly one engaged for an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a violin, but it is cheating, RIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Rigoletto is an opera about a hunchbacked jester.

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics

indicators.note: spoiled or ruined, the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Stress, as in wasted labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' scrambles AS IN to AINS.
explanation.definitionFit: To take pains is to make a careful effort.

indicators.note: taking a day off means removing it

parts.note: a wand is a rod or staff

explanation.surface: Ill employees are given a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, but it is a rod, WAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale and ill-looking, as a sickly face is.

clue.text: Unexpectedly going home, and happy about that

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: one piece placed around another

parts.note: content means satisfied, happy
that refers back to home, IN

explanation.surface: Someone leaving for home and pleased about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' refers back to 'home', so IN appears twice: IN + CONT(IN)ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking bladder control, so one may go to the lavatory unexpectedly.
